app.ramAsync: ({usableMB} MB − {workers} workers × {workerMemMB} MB) / {memMB} MB = {concurrency} in flight, each for {inFlightMs} ms
app.ramSync: {usableMB} MB / ({workerMemMB} + {memMB} MB per worker) = {fit} workers fit, each busy {inFlightMs} ms per request
app.workers: {workers} workers, one request each, busy {inFlightMs} ms per request

warnings.lbRequired: Only 1 of {count} servers gets traffic: without a load balancer, clients can only reach one.
warnings.connectionsExceeded: {servers} servers × {workers} workers × {pool} connections = {needed}, but the database allows {max}. The extra connections are refused.
warnings.idleCores: Only {workers} of {vcpu} vCPUs are used: each worker process runs on one core at a time. Add workers to use the rest.
warnings.workersDontFit: Only {fit} of {workers} workers fit in {ramGB} GB of RAM. The rest would be killed for running out of memory.

oneVps.name: One VPS
oneVps.desc: One app server and one database. Each request makes 3 queries, so the database runs out of CPU first, at about 167 req/s.

addCache.name: Add a cache
addCache.desc: 85% of reads now come from the cache, cutting database load by three quarters. The bottleneck moves to the app server's CPU.

scaleOut.name: Scale out
scaleOut.desc: A load balancer spreads traffic over 4 servers. The app tier can take 800 req/s, so the database is the limit again.

readReplicas.name: Read replicas
readReplicas.desc: Two replicas take the reads, but each still replays every write. With the primary only handling writes, the replicas become the limit.

blackFriday.name: Black Friday
blackFriday.desc: Traffic jumps 5×. Most requests fail. Try a CDN, more servers and more replicas to survive it.

async.name: Async
async.desc: Each worker juggles many requests at once (Node.js, FastAPI with async code).

sync.name: Sync
sync.desc: Each worker handles one request at a time (Gunicorn sync workers, PHP-FPM, Unicorn).
